title: awf-net subnet collides with host or cluster DNS resolver or routes
symptoms: Every CONNECT fails with 503 HIER_NONE after startup on OpenShift or ARO
The awf-net subnet contains the DNS resolver(s)
The awf-net subnet overlaps existing host route(s)
conditions: The default awf-net subnet 172.30.0.0/24 sits inside a cluster service CIDR (for example 172.30.0.0/16) whose CoreDNS ClusterIP is 172.30.0.10, the address AWF assigns to Squid
A nameserver from --dns-servers or the host resolv.conf falls inside the awf-net subnet, or a non-Docker host route overlaps it
Routes owned by Docker bridges (br-, docker, veth, awf, fw-bridge) are ignored by the collision check; the default route is ignored
rootCause: The awf-net subnet and Squid address were hardcoded to 172.30.0.0/24 and 172.30.0.10. Squid templated its DNS nameserver from the host resolver, so a resolver inside the subnet made Squid query its own peer address and every CONNECT failed. Relocation via --network-subnet and a fail-loud startup check remove the silent breakage.

probe.command: grep -n nameserver /etc/resolv.conf; cat /proc/net/route; docker network inspect awf-net --format '{{json .IPAM.Config}}'
probe.expect: Compare resolver addresses and any awf-net subnet with the chosen --network-subnet, and decode destination/mask entries in /proc/net/route to check for overlapping non-Docker host routes. Resolver and Docker network output alone cannot rule out a route conflict; Docker bridge routes and the default route are ignored by the collision check. These reads expose no credentials.

action: Relocate the network to a free RFC1918 block with --network-subnet (config key network.subnet), for example --network-subnet 10.88.0.0/24, and re-run. Do not disable the collision check or switch off DNS filtering. The check reports a collision as a startup error, so an error is the expected signal rather than a defect in the current code.
